title: Developer Oncall Field Manual — Status Scripts & Postmortem Cadence
author: Marcus Nguyen
body:
Overview
--------
This manual is a compact, developer-focused reference for first responders and bridge operators who run, stabilize, and close incidents affecting inference traffic. It combines:
- A concise incident lifecycle that matches our incident tooling and status page model.
- Reusable Slack + status-page message templates for internal and customer communication.
- Practical runbook actions for common LLM-serving degradations (latency SLO regressions, 5xx bursts, KV-cache storms, and throttling).
- A lightweight postmortem cadence and evidence checklist to ensure corrective action and measurable risk reduction.

Why this doc exists
- Reduce cognitive load for developer-oncall: follow-step guidance with safe defaults.
- Standardize external messaging to avoid conflicting customer updates.
- Make post-incident learning reliable: evidence captured during the first hour so root causes are reproducible.

Ownership & contact matrix
------------------------
- Primary owner (oncall bridge): Bridge Conductor (role).
- Primary technical responder: Service Owner oncall (team-specific pager).
- Escalation: Runtime Engineering (pager), SRE Escalation (pager).
- Executive notification: Director of Eng (on severe incidents only).

Quick contact (for bridge operator)
Role | Primary | Backup
-----|---------|-------
Bridge Conductor | marcos-bridge@redwood.ai | ops-bot@redwood.ai
Service Owner | svc-owner@redwood.ai | team-oncall@redwood.ai
Runtime Eng | runtime-pager@redwood.ai | runtime-backup@redwood.ai
SRE Escalation | sre-lead@redwood.ai | sre-oncall@redwood.ai

Incident lifecycle (concise)
---------------------------
1) Detect
   - Signals: SLO alert, synthetic failure, external customer report, monitoring anomaly.
   - Default detection channel: PagerDuty -> Slack #incidents -> start bridge.
2) Acknowledge (first 10 minutes)
   - Bridge Conductor acknowledges incident in PagerDuty and posts initial status.
   - Triage with Service Owner to classify impact (P0/P1/P2).
3) Stabilize (first 60 minutes)
   - Apply pre-approved mitigations from runbooks.
   - If mitigation reduces customer impact, escalate to restoration.
4) Restore
   - Apply permanent or near-term fixes (rollbacks, config flips, capacity augment).
   - Monitor SLOs and customer signals.
5) Postmortem & Corrective Actions
   - 24h quick blameless summary; 7-day deep postmortem for P0/P1 incidents.

Severity definitions & SLAs (selected)
------------------------------------
- P0: Platform-wide outage affecting >= 10% of production tokens or persistent > 30s request latency for > 5% of requests for 15+ minutes.
- P1: Significant degradation for a subset of customers or sustained error-rate increase > 3% above baseline for 10+ minutes.
- P2: Localized impact, single-region or tenant, intermittent errors or performance blips.

SLO examples (for runtime teams)
Metric | Target | Alert threshold
-------|--------|----------------
Gen latency (p95, 2k tokens) | <= 350ms | p95 > 450ms for 5m
End-to-end 5xx rate | <= 0.5% | 5xx > 1.5% for 3m
KV cache miss ratio | <= 8% | miss ratio > 15% for 10m

Runbook: Rapid KV cache storm (common failure pattern)
----------------------------------------------------
Goal: Reduce fanout and restore tail latency while preserving customer throughput.
Steps:
1. Confirm: check cache miss ratio + recent redeploys.
   - Metrics: cache_miss_ratio (dash), latency_p95_by_model.
2. Short-term (first 5-15m): enable per-model conservative caching policy.
   - CLI: rcli cache set-policy --model <model> --policy conservative
3. Reduce batching window for affected workers (reduces tail latency).
   - k8s: kubectl -n runtime patch deploy worker-<pool> --patch '{\"spec\":{\"template\":{\"spec\":{\"containers\":[{\"name\":\"worker\",\"env\":[{\"name\":\"BATCH_WINDOW_MS\",\"value\":\"50\"}] }]}}}}'
4. If CPU saturates: divert traffic to smaller sequence-length tuned model variant.
   - Routing command: rcli route set --service inference --model <model>-latency-variant
5. If instability persists >30m, engage Runtime Eng for emergency capacity scale (add GPU pool).

Runbook: 5xx burst (model OOM or library crash)
---------------------------------------------
1. Identify top failing path: Sentry + access logs.
2. If model OOM suspected, set fallback-mode: use quantized variant and pin instance reuse:
   - rcli runtime set --fallback-model <model>-q4 --reuse-kv true
3. If crash on new deploy: roll back to last known-good image.
   - k8s: kubectl rollout undo deploy/inference-service --to-revision=<rev>
4. Post-restore: increase crashloop backoff and mark deploy for postmortem.

Safe internal messaging (first 10 minutes)
----------------------------------------
- Bridge message (Slack #incidents):
  "INCIDENT | [P0/P1] | <short summary>\n   Bridge: @bridge-conductor-name\n   Impact: <high-level customer-facing impact>\n   Next update: in 15 minutes or when customer-visible state changes."

- Pager/owner ack snippet:
  "Acknowledged. Triage in progress. Primary lead: @svc-owner. Running runbook: <name>."

Customer-facing status page templates
------------------------------------
Use the short template for the first public notice; expand in subsequent updates.
1) Initial public status (short):
   "Redwood Inference is investigating elevated errors affecting text-generation requests in us-west-2. We are actively triaging and will provide updates within 15 minutes. Impact: a subset of customers may experience increased latency or 5xx responses."
2) Follow-up status (if mitigated):
   "We have identified a KV cache warm-up pattern causing tail latency. We applied conservative caching and reduced batch windows; error rates have decreased. We are monitoring; no customer action required. ETA for full restoration: 1-2 hours."
3) Post-incident summary (public):
   "Incident on YYYY-MM-DD caused by a cache storm triggered by a model routing change. Mitigations included policy rollback and conservative caching. Root cause analysis and mitigation plan published (internal)."

Slack templates (bridge -> cs/comm)
---------------------------------
- For CS teams (internal):
  "CS-ALERT: [INCIDENT P1] <short summary>. Expected customer impact: <list>. Suggested response lines: <one-sentence guidance>. Contact bridge: @bridge-conductor."
- For Execs (private channel):
  "Exec Notice: P0 incident impacting production inference (start: <time>, scope: <percent tokens>). Remediation in progress. Will escalate if > 90 minutes."

Postmortem cadence & artifact checklist
--------------------------------------
- P0/P1: 7-day deep postmortem required. 24-hour blameless incident summary published to #postmortems within 24h.
- P2: Quick 72h summary with owner action item list.

Required postmortem evidence (must be attached)
- PagerDuty timeline export (CSV)
- Bridge Slack transcript (first 24 minutes)
- Monitoring graphs: latency p50/p95/p99, error-rate, cache miss ratio for the affected timeframe
- Deploy history (git SHA + k8s revision)
- Synthetic test results run across affected endpoints

Postmortem template (short)
- Title, Impact summary, Detection timeline, Root cause, Mitigation, Action items (owner + due date), Postmortem author, Triage reviewer.

On-call rotation & human factors guidance
----------------------------------------
- Standard rotation: 7-day oncall for engineers. Short swaps allowed with 48h notice and replacement documented on the rota.
- Shadowing: 2-week shadow window for new oncallers.
- Handover: at shift start, the previous oncaller must post a 10-line summary: outstanding tickets, ongoing experiments, flagged deploys.
- Burnout safeguards: max 3 consecutive weeks as primary oncall. Temporary augment budget available (1 engineer/day) for high-severity incidents lasting >72h.

Game days and simulation design (recommended)
-------------------------------------------
- Cadence: quarterly game days per team; 2 focused scenarios per game day (one KV-cache-style, one capacity-throttle).
- Objectives: validate runbook actions under stress, verify bridge messaging templates, measure MTTR and evidence capture.
- Scoring (simple): 
  - Detection time (0-10) 
  - Acknowledge & bridge up (0-10)
  - First mitigation applied (0-10)
  - Evidence completeness (0-10)
  - Customer messaging accuracy (0-10)
- Post-game deliverable: improvement backlog + 1 targeted automation (e.g., auto-cache-policy flip, synthetic alert refinement).

Runbook hygiene & governance
---------------------------
- Every runbook must have: owner, last-run timestamp, last-validation timestamp.
- Validation: runbook dry-run during team game day at least once every 6 months.
- Decommission: runbooks not executed or validated for 18 months must be archived and reviewed before reuse.

Escalation SLA (internal)
------------------------
- P0: bridge up within 5 minutes, Runtime Eng oncall paged within 7 minutes.
- P1: bridge up within 10 minutes, Service Owner paged within 15 minutes.
- P2: triage within 30 minutes.

Appendices
---------
A) Commands quick reference
- rcli cache set-policy --model <model> --policy conservative
- rcli route set --service inference --model <model>-latency-variant
- kubectl rollout undo deploy/inference-service --to-revision=<rev>
- rcli runtime set --fallback-model <model>-q4 --reuse-kv true

B) Customer messaging examples (copy-paste-ready)
- Initial: "We’re investigating increased error rates affecting generation in <region>. We will update in 15 minutes."
- Mid-incident: "Mitigation applied. Error rates decreased by ~80% vs peak; monitoring to confirm full restoration (ETA 1–2h)."
- Closure public: "Root cause identified as a cache warming pattern; mitigation plan implemented. We will roll out a permanent fix by <date>. Contact support@redwood.ai for tenant-specific impact."

C) Postmortem owner rotation (process)
- The service owner assigns a postmortem author within 48 hours. If unassigned, Bridge Conductor defaults as author.
- Action items must have owners and target completion dates; overdue items reviewed at weekly reliability sync.

------------
